questions.question: Which of the following best describes the evolution of the principle of 'cuius regio, eius religio' from the Peace of Augsburg (1555) to the Peace of Westphalia (1648)?
options: It mandated that Holy Roman Emperors must be chosen through an equal vote of Protestant and Catholic electors.
It expanded the legally recognized confessions within the Holy Roman Empire to include Calvinism alongside Lutheranism and Catholicism.
It stripped territorial princes of the right to determine state religion, transferring that authority directly to local municipal councils.
It abolished the concept of state religion entirely, guaranteeing absolute individual religious freedom across Western Europe.

questions.question: Under the Canton System established by the Qing Dynasty in 1757, European maritime trade with China was restricted to which specific legal and operational framework?
options: Trading exclusively through a licensed guild of Chinese merchants known as the Cohong in the single port city of Guangzhou.
Conducting direct diplomatic and commercial negotiations with imperial officials in Beijing.
Operating freely across five designated treaty ports under European consular legal jurisdiction.
Utilizing paper currency issued by the Grand Canal Administration to purchase silk and tea directly from inland producers.

questions.question: What was a defining socio-ideological feature of the mid-nineteenth-century Taiping Rebellion led by Hong Xiuquan?
options: An orthodox Confucian movement dedicated to restoring the Ming Dynasty's scholar-bureaucracy.
A Daoist peasant insurrection focused on eliminating foreign technology and reverting to agrarian isolation.
A pro-Western military coup bankrolled by European commercial interests to establish a constitutional monarchy.
A syncretic movement combining heterodox Christian theology with radical social egalitarianism, land redistribution, and prohibitions against foot binding and opium.

questions.question: During the reign of Askia Muhammad I (Askia the Great) in the late 15th and early 16th centuries, the Songhai Empire achieved its peak institutional coherence primarily through:
options: The abandonment of trans-Saharan trade routes in favor of exclusive maritime commerce with Portuguese coastal factories.
The total rejection of Islamic administrative models in favor of regional ancestral cult governance.
The centralization of provincial governance, standardization of trade weights and measures, and official patronage of Islamic scholarship in urban centers like Timbuktu.
The submission of the empire as a formal tributary vassal state to the Ottoman Regency of Algiers.

questions.question: The 'sankin-kōtai' (alternate attendance) system implemented by the Tokugawa Shogunate functioned primarily as a political tool to:
options: Recruit Dutch and Portuguese mercenaries to modernize the Shogunate's standing army.
Control regional daimyo by forcing them to spend alternate years in Edo and leave their families behind as political hostages, thereby draining their financial resources.
Select imperial succession candidates through competitive military tournaments hosted at the court in Kyoto.
Enforce the universal conversion of the samurai class to Neo-Confucianism while suppressing Buddhist monastic orders.
